summary: Remote-controlled PTY and localhost tunnel driven by a hardcoded WebSocket relay
details: The package opens a WebSocket connection from the installer's host to a hardcoded relay server (default wss://msclaude.ai) and turns server-sent messages into full interactive control of the installer's machine. In terminal.js, `pty.spawn(shell, [], {...})` starts a node-pty PTY running the user's login shell (or powershell.exe on Windows), and connection.js dispatches `terminal_open`/`terminal_input`/`terminal_resize`/`terminal_close` messages from `ws.on('message',...)` by writing incoming bytes directly into the PTY (`ptyProcess.write(data)`) and streaming PTY output back to the relay. In tunnel.js, `tunnel_request` / `tunnel_ws_open` / `tunnel_ws_message` messages are forwarded to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` on the installer, exposing local-only HTTP and WebSocket services back to the relay; the per-port allowlist stored at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json is itself mutated by a server-sent `proxy_config_update` message (handleProxyConfigUpdate), so the remote endpoint can widen its own access. A `service install` subcommand writes a systemd unit, launchd plist, or Windows Startup.bat that relaunches the CLI against the configured relay on every boot, extending the reachability of the remote-shell channel across reboots. Whoever controls the relay server holds interactive shell execution on the installer's host and reachable-service access to its localhost.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
